sections.eyebrow: Prepared for Neysa's revenue & growth team
sections.headline: Agents that run your paid engine and *make the next move*.
sections.subhead: You run a high-velocity, two-channel program — 54 LinkedIn creatives driving event-led ABM, 21 Google search ads capturing GPU-pricing intent, and nothing on Meta by design. Agents watch both surfaces daily, catch where spend leaks or an ICP account stalls, and hand you the exact next move — with the reasoning behind it. You approve; they act.

card.title: H100 pricing ads show $0.52, $4.50 and ₹40/hr — three prices for one product
card.body: Across your live Google RSAs, the H100 hourly price varies by creative. Mixed price claims split intent and dilute the conquesting message.
card.move: Consolidate to one lead price on the top-converting term, and flag the disapproved creative before it burns more impressions.

sections.heading: We studied how Neysa runs paid *before writing a word*.
sections.body: Pulled from your public Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, July 2026. It's a high-velocity, deliberately India-led engine. Here's what we saw — and where an agent layer earns its keep.

channels.label: Ads — GPU-pricing intent capture
channels.body: H100 from $0.52/hr, ₹40/hr, 'Made in India, for India,' SOC 2 / ISO 27001. Pure bottom-of-funnel — you buy GPU-rental intent, not awareness. No YouTube; one Business Profile local ad.

channels.label: Creatives — event ABM + thought leadership
channels.body: Every format: the 'your model works in the lab, production is a scaling nightmare' essays, Velocis product videos, and event bursts (India AI Impact Summit, MTW 2026). This is your brand engine.

channels.label: Deliberately none
channels.body: No Facebook or Instagram ads. For an Indian enterprise + AI-native ICP reachable on Google intent and LinkedIn job targeting, that's the right call — a channel decision, not a gap.

sections.footer: The engine is dialed in. The gap isn't the ads — it's that the two channels run channel-by-channel: which accounts actually become pipeline, correlated across Google intent and every LinkedIn touch, and acted on daily. That's the layer Northstar Analytics owns.

sections.eyebrow: The one thing still running tool-by-tool
sections.heading: You gave AI teams their entire stack, finally unified. Your go-to-market spend is the one place that isn't.
sections.body: Velocis exists so teams stop stitching GPUs, MLOps and deployment by hand. But your own growth engine still runs the way most do — spend in Google and LinkedIn, pipeline in the CRM, and nobody joining them daily. Northstar Analytics closes that seam for your GTM the way Velocis closed it for AI infrastructure.

sections.heading: Point the agents at a goal. Agents run the rest.
sections.body: Set a goal in your own terms — cost-per-opportunity on GPU-intent search, enterprise pipeline by segment — and the agent works out what to watch and what to do, on your numbers.

goals.text: Cut cost-per-opportunity on GPU-pricing search 25% — without dropping trial volume.
goals.result: Agents watch every RSA daily and move budget toward the terms that produce opportunities, not just clicks.

goals.text: Get event-led LinkedIn ABM credited and converting — route every ICP account it warms.
goals.result: Agents learn the path your closed-won accounts took, catch the ones that stall, and hand them to sales before they cool.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.body: Track every Google and LinkedIn campaign and CRM event daily — against your goal and your own baseline, not a canned benchmark.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Every number is checked against source data before it reaches you — grounded analysis, not a guess.

steps.title: Recommend
steps.body: When a sustained pattern bears on the goal, surface the move in Slack: evidence, cause, action, and what it's worth.

steps.title: Act
steps.body: Approve and the agent acts — shifting budget, adding negatives, routing the account. Nothing fires until you say so.

steps.title: Learn
steps.body: Every call you make is graded into memory, so next month's recommendation fits your motion better than this one.

sections.heading: Always know your next move.
sections.body: One engine watches paid-media efficiency; the other watches ICP accounts against your golden path. Two live examples, built for Neysa.

cards.title: GPU-rental terms convert 3× cheaper than generic 'AI infrastructure' — but spend hasn't moved
cards.body: Over 21 days, generic 'AI infrastructure' terms drove volume but few opportunities, while 'H100 rent / price' terms converted at a fraction of the cost. The budget split between them hasn't changed in 90 days.
cards.move: Shift 25% of generic-term budget to the high-intent H100-pricing terms, add the zero-opp terms as exact-match negatives, and re-check in 14 days.

cards.title: 19 enterprise ICP accounts engaged your LinkedIn ABM twice — none are in the CRM
cards.body: Over 21 days, 19 Indian BFSI & AI-native accounts matching your named-account profile hit 2+ high-intent touches on LinkedIn and viewed pricing — but never entered Salesforce. This is the pattern behind 4 of your last 6 enterprise closed-won.
cards.move: Route the 9 enterprise accounts to sales this week as a named list, load all 19 into the LinkedIn ABM audience, and suppress them from cold outbound.
